titel: Osmosis: salt and sugar draw out water
kurz: Salt and sugar attract water. On a surface they pull moisture out from the inside.
bild_im_kopf: Like dry sand on a beach soaking up every wave: water moves to where there is a lot of salt.
was_passiert: Water moves to where there are more dissolved substances. Sprinkle [[salz|salt]] on meat or vegetables and after a short time juice seeps out and dissolves the salt. With meat, this salty solution soaks back in over time. With vegetables such as aubergines or cucumbers, you use it to get rid of water.
warum_wichtig: Explains why freshly salted meat looks wet and shiny, and why you either fry it straight away or wait a long time.
faustregeln: After about 10–40 minutes the surface is at its wettest: do not fry then, as a guide.
Squeeze out or pat dry salted vegetables before frying.

praxis.text: Salt right before frying or many hours ahead, not in between.
Salt aubergine or courgette slices, pat them dry, then fry: they soak up less oil.
